articles.body: A high-ranking Lashkar-e-Taiba operative is learnt to have died under mysterious circumstances, leaving many in Islamabad intrigued.Qari Saeed Abdul Aziz, who was involved in the planning of the 26/11 Mumbai terrorist attacks, collapsed and died near the entrance of a mosque in the Pakistan capital on August 8.Local media reports indicated Abdul Aziz had dined at an unfamiliar location shortly before arriving at the mosque.Within moments of reaching the gate, he suddenly collapsed and was pronounced dead on the spot, with the exact cause of his demise remaining unclear. articles.title: After weeks of violent protests, PoK votes in final election phase amid PTI, JAAC boycott calls
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Polling for Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir's so called assembly elections entered its final phase on Monday amid heightened security and reports .
articles.body: Polling for Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir's so called assembly elections entered its final phase on Monday amid heightened security and reports of Islamabad-backed crackdown in the region.Voting is being held despite boycott calls from the Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) PoJK unit and the Pakistan-banned Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC).The tussle between the JAAC and the Shehbaz Sharif-Asim Munir duo's crackdown has made the situation grim in PoK.India has also strongly condemned the crackdown on protesters. The MEA has called the so-called assembly elections in the illegally occupied region as a "farce".The MEA also condemned Pakistan's actions that led to the killing of 90 civilians in PoK.Meanwhile, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) PoJK unit has announced a complete boycott of the ongoing electoral process in Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir (PoJK), calling it “unconstitutional” and “unfair”.The election has taken place against the backdrop of weeks of protests led by the JAAC, which has been demanding greater political rights for residents of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.The final phase also came after media curbs, and other major restrictions imposed by Islamabad authority.The demonstrations have also seen clashes with security forces, overshadowing the election campaign.The ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) has already secured a majority in the assembly, seeing a likely return after a decade.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Russia warns UK over Ukraine drone supplies, says Britain will face ‘consequences’
articles.summary: Europe News: Russia warned Britain on Monday it would pay a 'price' for its support for Ukraine, including the reported supply of drones used in strikes deep insid.
articles.body: Russia warned Britain on Monday it would pay a 'price' for its support for Ukraine, including the reported supply of drones used in strikes deep inside Russian territory. The warning has further strained ties between Moscow and London amid escalating long-range drone attacks in the war.Russia’s embassy in London said British actions were making the country an “accomplice and co-perpetrator” in attacks on Russian territory and accused Britain of “deliberately opting for an escalation”.“London’s actions will inevitably carry consequences for which it will have to answer,” the embassy said in a statement posted on its Telegram channel.“The deeper its involvement in the conflict and the greater its support for Kiev’s terrorist machinery, the higher the price it will pay,” it said.The warning followed reports in the Times and Sunday Times that British-made drones had been used by Ukraine in long-range strikes against military and industrial targets inside Russia. The Sunday Times reported that one of the companies involved was a subsidiary of defence giant BAE Systems, while the second company was not identified for security reasons.Britain’s ministry of defence did not confirm whether British-made drones had been used in the strikes. Responding to the Russian embassy’s comments, a ministry spokesperson said, “Britain stands shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine and we are committed to providing the equipment Ukraine needs to defend itself against Putin’s illegal invasion.”Britain has remained one of Ukraine’s key military backers since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. London has committed around £25 billion in support, including £16 billion in military aid, while in June it announced plans to provide Ukraine with 150,000 drones by the end of 2026 as part of a £752 million funding package.The warning came as Ukraine intensified its long-range drone campaign against Russia.Moscow said Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks on the Russian capital and surrounding areas, with Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin saying 180 drones had been downed over the region. Regional governor Andrei Vorobyov separately said drones struck a Wildberries warehouse and other facilities, injuring at least three people, including a 10-year-old girl.Ukrainian forces also launched almost 800 drones at targets across Russia, according to Russian officials, two days after another large-scale drone attack.At the same time, Russian forces continued strikes on Ukraine. A Russian missile strike on a village in the northeastern Kharkiv region killed at least 10 people and wounded eight, Ukrainian officials said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: British couple on honeymoon die in helicopter crash on Greek island; pilot also killed
articles.summary: Europe News: A British couple were killed alongside their pilot when their private helicopter crashed on the Greek island of Sifnos on Monday, just minutes before .
articles.body: A British couple were killed alongside their pilot when their private helicopter crashed on the Greek island of Sifnos on Monday, just minutes before they were due to land at a heliport.Alexander Cromie and Marie Ebert were on their honeymoon when the helicopter went down in the Tholos area of Sifnos. Greek police said the couple and the pilot, 55-year-old Giorgos Raikos, died in the crash.The helicopter had flown from Markopoulo, a village southeast of Athens, to Sifnos and was scheduled to land at around 6:15pm local time, according to Greek media reports cited by the BBC.A senior police official said that the crash occurred shortly before the scheduled landing.Local residents reported hearing what Sifnos deputy mayor Manolis Foundoulakis described as a “bizarre engine noise” shortly before the helicopter went down. The aircraft crashed just metres from the landing area, caught fire and was largely destroyed.Emergency crews later extinguished the flames and recovered the victims from the wreckage and nearby area.The pilot was identified by Greek media as Giorgos Raikos, a former Hellenic Army veteran who later became a professional helicopter pilot. According to reports cited by People, Raikos had informed air traffic control that he was preparing to land shortly before the crash, after which radio contact was reportedly lost.The cause of the crash remains unknown. Aviation authorities are examining the circumstances, including flight records, weather conditions and the possibility of mechanical failure. Reports said weather conditions were normal at the time, with no strong winds.The UK Foreign Office said it was working with Greek authorities and was prepared to provide support to the couple's families. Greek authorities have opened an investigation into the crash.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Break Agnipath deadlock, Gorkha veterans press Balen govt as Indian Army chief visits Pokhara
articles.summary: South Asia News: Calls for Nepal to allow its citizens to join the Indian Army under its Agnipath scheme have grown louder ahead of Indian Army chief General Dhiraj Se.
articles.body: Calls for Nepal to allow its citizens to join the Indian Army under its Agnipath scheme have grown louder ahead of Indian Army chief General Dhiraj Seth’s scheduled participation in an ex-servicemen rally for Gorkha veterans in Pokhara on Wednesday, bringing the stalled recruitment issue back into focus during his three-day Nepal visit.Days before Gen Seth's arrival, hundreds of former Indian Army personnel, their families and Gorkha aspirants marched in Pokhara, urging Nepal prime minister Balen Shah to permit recruitment under Agnipath. The rally was organised by Indian Ex-Servicemen Gorkha Brigade Nepal, which submitted a memorandum to Shah and home minister Sudan Gurung.The recruitment deadlock has remained an unresolved backdrop to Gen Seth’s visit, though official accounts of his talks with Nepal Army chief General Ashok Raj Sigdel have made no mention of the issue. Gen Seth was conferred the honorary rank of General of the Nepal Army by President Ramchandra Paudel on Monday, continuing a decades-old reciprocal military tradition between the two countries.Gen Seth met Shah in Kathmandu on Tuesday, but the official statement stayed with familiar phrases on "defence cooperation and military ties". Agnipath found no public mention.Colonel Krishna Bahadur Khatri (retd), chairman of the organisation, told TOI from Kathmandu that Nepal’s stand had "deprived its youths of an opportunity still seen by many Gorkha families as far better than low-paid employment overseas". He added: “After India introduced the Agnipath scheme, Nepal govt, citing various reasons, deprived Nepalese youths of the opportunity to join Indian Army,” Khatri said. In its memorandum, the organisation said, “We once again request govt to immediately restart the process of recruiting Nepalese youths into Indian Army under the Agnipath policy. This profession is hundreds of times better than going to the Gulf, working in temperatures of 50 degrees Celsius and receiving minimum wages.”Retired Captain Rudra Thapa said the freeze had pushed many young men from Gorkha families towards low-paid, physically demanding jobs in the Gulf and other countries when they could have earned a far higher and more stable income through military service. “Our youths are going abroad for menial jobs, working in harsh conditions and earning very little. If they were allowed to join Indian Army as Agniveers, they could have earned around Nepalese Rs 45-50 lakh, including benefits, in four years,” Thapa said. “If govt does not permit recruitment into foreign armies, it must be able to provide employment at home.”A similar appeal was made last month by Lamjung Indian Ex-Servicemen Development Committee. In a memorandum signed by its chairman Chitra Bahadur Gurung, the committee said the prolonged freeze had cost thousands of youths employment, created uncertainty among Gorkha families and weakened one of the oldest institutional links between Nepal and India.India introduced Agnipath in June 2022, under which recruits serve for four years and up to 25% may later be absorbed into regular service. Nepal declined to allow recruitment under the new terms, arguing that the four-year contractual model marked a departure from the long-term service and pension arrangement that underpinned the 1947 tripartite agreement between Nepal, India and Britain. No Nepal-domiciled Gorkhas have been recruited since Nepal put the process on hold in 2022.The deadlock matters because Nepal-domiciled Gorkhas have long formed an important part of the Indian Army’s Gorkha regiments. Nepalese soldiers constitute about 60% of each battalion, while Indians make up the rest. Around 12,000 Gorkha soldiers from Nepal have retired since 2021, but no fresh Nepal-domiciled recruitment has taken place to replace them after Nepal blocked the first round of recruitment in July 2022, followed by later rounds.Kathmandu has also raised concerns that 75% of Agniveers who are released after four years could return home without jobs or pension despite military training. Indian officials, however, have maintained that Agnipath is now the only recruitment route into the Indian Army and that resumption of Nepal-domiciled Gorkha recruitment depends on Nepal’s consent.There has been some softening in Kathmandu’s tone under the Shah govt. During a visit to New Delhi in June, Nepalese foreign minister Shisir Khanal said the issue had not figured in his formal discussions but indicated willingness to engage. “The recruitment used to be done through a tripartite agreement. In the most recent conversations, we have not gone into those dialogues and discussions,” Khanal said. Asked whether Nepal would reopen talks, he added, “If India wants, we can discuss.” Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'We'll bomb the s*** out of them': Why Trump is again threatening Oman amid Iran talks
articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trump has again threatened to strike Oman, accusing the Gulf nation of potentially standing in the way of an agreement with Iran, .
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has again threatened to strike Oman, accusing the Gulf nation of potentially standing in the way of an agreement with Iran, as negotiations over the future of the Strait of Hormuz remain stalled and a 60-day US-Iran interim arrangement expires without a permanent deal.Trump’s latest warning came as Oman and Iran moved closer to an understanding on the reopening and management of commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway through which about one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas supplies passed before the war.“If Oman gets in the way, we'll bomb the s*** out of them,” Trump told Fox News on Monday, according to Reuters.The threat places Oman, a longstanding US partner and one of Washington's traditional channels for communicating with Tehran, at the centre of the growing dispute over the strait. It also marks the second time in recent months that Trump has threatened military action against Oman over the issue.Trump says Iran must surrenderTrump's warning came as his administration's efforts to secure a broader agreement with Iran appeared to have stalled. Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office on Monday, Trump said Tehran would not accept the agreement he believed was necessary to end the conflict.“They're not going to make the kind of a deal that I feel is necessary. Look, we're in there for one reason: Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon,” he told reporters.Asked whether Washington was seeking an extension of the interim agreement with Tehran, Trump said "no."Earlier on Monday, Trump had told Fox News that Iran should surrender and put pressure on Tehran to accept Washington's terms.The US president also repeated on Truth Social that preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon remained his administration's central objective."The number one Goal is, and always will be, that Iran cannot have, in any way, shape, or form, a Nuclear Weapon," Trump wrote.The latest developments came on the day the 60-day period under a US-Iran memorandum of understanding was due to expire. The agreement had committed both sides to negotiating a final arrangement covering broader issues, including Iran's nuclear programme.However, the arrangement quickly unravelled. Trump declared it "over" on July 7, while Iran's foreign ministry said a week later that it had been "suspended".Why Oman is now at the centreOman's role in the crisis is closely linked to the Strait of Hormuz, which separates Iran from Oman and has become one of the most important pressure points in the conflict.Iran and Oman have been negotiating a mechanism to restore commercial shipping through the strait after the earlier US-Iran arrangement broke down.On Monday, Iranian officials said Tehran and Muscat had reached an understanding on a new shipping route and were preparing a joint declaration. Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the proposed arrangement would seek to protect the interests of both countries while allowing commercial vessels to pass safely.“This is the first time that a mechanism is being developed to simultaneously safeguard the sovereign rights of the two littoral states and ensure the safe passage of commercial vessels,” Baghaei said.The proposed arrangement has alarmed Washington because it could give Iran and Oman a greater role in determining how ships move through the waterway.For the Trump administration, the issue is not simply about reopening the strait. Washington has demanded that Iran relinquish control over shipping routes and has opposed any arrangement that could allow Tehran to impose charges on vessels.US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has warned that Iran must not be allowed to impose tolls on ships using the strait.Trump has also said there should be no tolls for vessels passing through Hormuz unless they are collected by the United States.Trump had threatened Oman beforeTrump's latest warning is not the first time he has threatened Oman over the Strait of Hormuz.In May, he was asked about a proposal under which Iran and Oman would jointly oversee shipping through the waterway.“Nobody is going to control it. It’s international waters, and Oman will behave just like everybody else, or we will have to blow them up,” Trump said at the time.There was initially speculation that Trump might have meant Iran rather than Oman. However, the US State Department later published the remarks along with a transcript that explicitly referred to Oman.The latest threat therefore marks a renewed escalation in Trump's rhetoric towards a country that has historically maintained close relations with Washington while also preserving diplomatic channels with Tehran.Oman caught between US and IranOman has traditionally followed a policy of neutrality in regional conflicts and has played an important role in facilitating communication between the US and Iran.The country has longstanding defence and economic ties with Washington, including security cooperation and a free trade agreement. At the same time, Muscat has maintained close diplomatic relations with Tehran.That position has allowed Oman to act as a mediator in previous US-Iran disputes.Its role has become more complicated since the conflict began. Iran has targeted US military assets and infrastructure across the region, while Oman has sought to prevent the Strait of Hormuz from becoming permanently closed to commercial shipping.Oman has not publicly aligned itself with either side in the dispute over the waterway.Its current talks with Iran are focused on restoring commercial traffic and establishing a mechanism for ships to safely navigate the strait.But any arrangement that gives Iran a formal role in determining shipping routes could conflict with Washington's demands.Why the Strait of Hormuz mattersThe Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most strategically important maritime chokepoints.Before the conflict began, roughly one-fifth of global oil and LNG supplies moved through the waterway. Around 130 ships passed through the strait each day, according to the background material cited in the reports.The conflict has sharply disrupted that traffic.Iran closed the strait in early March, allowing only vessels it considered friendly to pass. Shipping briefly improved after the June US-Iran memorandum, but tensions over the routes used by commercial vessels soon triggered fresh confrontation.Iran later refused to resume direct negotiations with Washington, arguing that the US had violated the terms of the agreement by continuing military operations.The dispute has also affected energy markets. Brent crude, which was trading around $66 a barrel before the conflict, has risen sharply during periods of heightened tension, at times crossing $100.Brent crude futures stood at $91.22 a barrel on Tuesday, according to the source material, close to a three-week high.US blockade adds to pressureWashington has also established a blockade around Iranian ports in and near the Strait of Hormuz.Last week, US forces fired on a Panama-flagged cargo vessel that Washington accused of attempting to reach Iranian ports and failing to comply with orders to change course.The confrontation has created another obstacle to reopening the waterway.Iran wants guarantees against further US attacks and has demanded sanctions relief as part of any broader settlement. Washington, meanwhile, wants Iran's nuclear programme curtailed and the strait fully reopened without Iranian control over commercial passage.Oman's attempt to bridge those positions has put Muscat in an increasingly difficult position.Why Trump is angry with OmanThe Trump administration appears divided over Oman's role.Some US officials have accused Oman of being too accommodating towards Iran and fear that a Tehran-Muscat agreement could produce terms more favourable to Iran.Others view Oman's longstanding relationship with Tehran as an advantage because it gives Muscat access to Iranian officials and allows it to mediate when direct US-Iran talks are not possible.The emerging Iran-Oman arrangement could also undermine Washington's negotiating position if it establishes a separate mechanism for managing the strait without direct US involvement.Trump has already complained that allies and partners are not doing enough to support his campaign against Iran.The issue has also taken on a domestic political dimension, with rising fuel prices and pressure over the economic impact of the conflict as the November US midterm elections approach. Trump has denied that the elections are influencing his Iran strategy."Midterms have nothing to do with my thinking," he told Fox News.Trump wants control of the strait issue resolvedTrump has also taken a more direct position on the future status of the Strait of Hormuz.Earlier this month, he said he would consider declaring the waterway US territory after claiming that Iran was being defeated.“After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated, pretty soon I’ll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States,” Trump said on August 14.Iran rejected the suggestion.Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the strait could not be taken over through a social media post, an aircraft carrier or a political declaration, and said Iran was not intimidated by US military power.The disagreement reflects the larger dispute behind Trump's latest threat to Oman. For Washington, reopening Hormuz is tied to limiting Iran's ability to use the waterway as leverage. For Tehran, control over navigation through waters adjoining its territory remains linked to sovereignty, security and its broader demands for an end to US military action.Oman is now attempting to negotiate a path between those competing positions.For Trump, however, any agreement that allows Iran and Oman to determine the future of the strait without US approval risks becoming another obstacle to the deal he wants with Tehran. His latest threat shows how the dispute over a narrow waterway has evolved into a much broader confrontation involving Iran's nuclear programme, US military strategy, global energy supplies and the diplomatic role of one of Washington's traditional Gulf partners.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Quote of the Day by Ernest Hemingway, "Happiness in intelligent people is the....."
articles.summary: Ernest Hemingway was among the most influential American writers of the 20th century. His novels and short stories changed modern literature with thei.
articles.body: Ernest Hemingway was among the most influential American writers of the 20th century. His novels and short stories changed modern literature with their lean prose, understated emotion and memorable characters. He wrote about war, love, masculinity, courage, adventure, loss and death, but behind the apparent simplicity of his language lay a profoundly complex understanding of human nature. Hemingway was born on July 21, 1899, in Oak Park, Illinois, into a fairly comfortable family. His father, Clarence Hemingway, was a physician; his mother, Grace Hall Hemingway, a musician and teacher. From a young age, Hemingway took an interest in writing and the outdoors. After graduating from high school, he went to work for the Kansas City Star as a reporter. The newspaper's style guide, it is said, called for short sentences, clear language and energetic writing – the principles that would later become central to Hemingway's literary style.His life was transformed during World War I. He volunteered for the Red Cross in 1918 as an ambulance driver in Italy. He was seriously wounded by mortar fire while in Italy and spent months recovering. His wartime experience had a powerful influence on his writing, particularly his understanding of courage, trauma and disillusionment. After the war Hemingway moved to Paris and joined a remarkable community of writers and artists. He moved among characters like Gertrude Stein, F. Scott Fitzgerald, Ezra Pound and James Joyce. These were significant years for the development of his writing.In his memoir A Moveable Feast, published later, Hemingway described the writers and artists he met in Paris. The experience also helped shape his identity as part of the Lost Generation, a group of writers who came of age during or after World War I and often struggled with the disillusionment of the time.A new way to writeHemingway’s style was perhaps his greatest contribution.In a time when literary prose could be elaborate and very descriptive, Hemingway often did the reverse. His sentences were short, pointed, economical. He never explained unnecessarily, he relied on readers to understand what his characters were feeling from what they did and said.This was the "iceberg theory" or the theory of omission. The idea was that a writer should only show a small part of the story directly, But like an iceberg, most of its meaning lies below the surface. A character might say very little about grief or fear or love, but the reader can feel huge emotion behind it. It made Hemingway’s writing seem deceptively simple. His sentences were often easy to read, but his stories were not necessarily easy to comprehend. His style is evident in his first novel, The Sun Also Rises (1926), which tells of the wanderings of expatriates through Europe after the First World War. The book caught the restlessness and disillusionment of a generation. He followed it up with A Farewell to Arms (1929), which was based heavily on his experiences in wartime Italy. The novel blended love and war and looked at the destructive effects of violence.The Sea and the WriterHemingway’s interest in courage, endurance and nature perhaps found its purest expression in The Old Man and the Sea (1952). This novella is about Santiago, an old Cuban fisherman who has a hard time catching a giant marlin. The story is simple on the surface, but underneath is a meditation on dignity, perseverance, ageing, defeat and human resilience. Hemingway won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1953 for the work. A year later he won the Nobel Prize for Literature.His mastery of narrative art and his impact on the contemporary style were cited by the Nobel committee.Hemingway’s life of adventureHemingway wasn’t just a writer of adventure, he was a seeker of it. He travelled extensively, lived in Europe and Cuba, went on African safaris, fished, hunted and witnessed major historical events. He was also a correspondent in the Spanish Civil War and later covered World War II.His experiences found their way into his fiction over and over. He was interested in bullfighting, big-game hunting and deep-sea fishing, and those subjects turned up in all his writing. His public image, too, was fused inextricably with ideas of toughness, of independence and of masculine courage.Yet Hemingway’s sense of courage was more complex than his outsized persona might suggest. His characters often find themselves in circumstances beyond their own control. They are not necessarily strong in winning but in holding to dignity in the face of suffering or defeat.His Influence on LiteratureHemingway revolutionised the way generations of writers wrote prose. His influence is seen in journalism, fiction, screenwriting and popular storytelling. Writers learned from his ability to create powerful scenes without over-explaining.But his impact was not confined to literature. The image of Hemingway the traveller, fisherman, war correspondent and writer entered popular culture. But his legacy has its critics too. His personal life was also complicated, with multiple marriages, physical injuries, alcoholism, and periods of serious emotional distress. Hemingway died in Ketchum, Idaho, on July 2, 1961, at the age of 61.And more than six decades after his death, his writing continues to be read because of something extraordinarily hard to do: he made simplicity powerful. His stories remind us that courage is not always a grand thing, that pain can hide behind everyday talk, and that a person's character is often shown not in what they say, but in what they do when life is hard. Perhaps Hemingway’s greatest lesson as a writer is in the space between his words, in what he deliberately left unsaid.Quote of the DayOne of the most iconic lines of Ernest Hemingway are, "Happiness in intelligent people is the rarest thing I know." What Hemingway says hints at something more profound than the idea that intelligent people are condemned to unhappiness. He is speaking of the link between intelligence, consciousness and happiness.The intelligent man often sees more than what is immediately before him. They see contradictions, uncertainty, injustice, disappointment and complexity of human behaviour. The problem may be ignored by someone, but the analytical mind keeps asking Why? What if... What is this?That constant awareness can make simple happiness hard to come by.An intelligent person can also overthink. They may not just have a moment, they may analyse a moment. They may not accept a situation, but rather question it. Rather than enjoying their success, they may start to think about what could go wrong next. They seldom have a completely still mind.Then there is the issue of expectations. The more you know about the world, the more clearly you can see the gap between what the world is and what it could be. They may come to understand that relationships aren't perfect, success is fleeting and life has its share of suffering along with the joy. Such a consciousness can make happiness appear fragile.But the point of Hemingway’s observation is that “intelligent people cannot be happy.” It implies that maybe happiness requires something that intelligence alone cannot provide: the ability to stop thinking and experience life.Sometimes happiness is about things that do not need an intellectual solution, a conversation with someone we love, sunlight on a quiet morning, a meal shared with friends, music, nature or just being present.Here is an interesting paradox: the intelligence that brings awareness of the problems of life can also bring understanding of what really matters.Or perhaps that’s the quote’s real meaning. Happiness does not necessarily mean the absence of hard thoughts. It’s that ability to live with those thoughts, without letting them destroy every moment of joy.”In that sense, Hemingway’s line is less about the curse of intelligence and more about the difficulty in finding peace when your mind just won’t stop thinking.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.body: MacKenzie Scott is now known for giving billions of dollars to charities, but her own experience of needing financial help began much earlier. While studying at Princeton, Scott faced a difficult period when money was tight and remaining at university was uncertain. Her roommate, Jeannie Ringo Tarkenton, noticed her struggle and lent her $1,000, helping Scott continue her education. That single act of generosity from a college friend would eventually inspire Scott's own remarkable transformation into one of history's most generous philanthropic figures.At the time, it was simply a friend helping another student through a difficult moment. Scott later remembered the gesture as one of the acts of kindness that shaped her outlook on giving. The story took an unexpected turn years later when Tarkenton went on to create Funding U, a company offering education loans to students who may struggle to qualify for traditional private loans. What began as a modest loan between roommates eventually became part of a much larger story about education, financial support and philanthropy. The experience gave Scott a personal connection to the difference that timely financial support can make when someone’s future depends on being able to stay in education. That early experience appears to have reinforced the idea that even a relatively small act of support can alter the course of someone’s life.MacKenzie Scott remembers the roommate who helped her stay in college with $1,000Scott arrived at Princeton with ambitions that would eventually take her into both literature and business. Money, however, could become a serious problem. During her sophomore year, she was struggling financially and faced the possibility of leaving university.According to Fortune, her roommate, Jeannie Ringo Tarkenton, noticed what was happening. Rather than treating it as someone else’s problem, she lent Scott $1,000. It was a relatively small amount compared with the fortunes Scott would later give away, but its significance was tied to the timing. The money helped Scott continue her studies at a point when an interruption could have changed the direction of her life.Scott has since described the incident as one of several acts of kindness she remembers when considering the people who influenced her. In an essay published through Yield Giving, she also recalled receiving free dental treatment from a local dentist after breaking a tooth while she was at college.Those experiences became part of her understanding of how assistance can work. Help does not always arrive as a large grant or a formal programme. Sometimes it comes from a person who happens to be nearby when someone needs it.From Toni Morrison’s student to a novelist: Scott’s career took a major turn after 2019Scott graduated from Princeton and went into writing, studying under the novelist Toni Morrison. Her literary career preceded the period when she became widely known for philanthropy.In 2005, she published The Testing of Luther Albright, her first novel. The book later received the American Book Award, and Morrison praised it for its emotional and literary qualities.Her career took a very different turn in the public eye after her marriage to Jeff Bezos ended in 2019. As part of the divorce settlement, Scott received a substantial holding in Amazon, giving her the financial resources to become a major philanthropist.The scale of her giving grew rapidly. Since 2020, she has directed billions of dollars towards organisations working across areas such as education, racial and gender equity, disaster recovery and community development.How a $1,000 loan grew into a mission to help studentsTarkenton did not simply remain a footnote in Scott’s story. About two decades after lending her roommate the money, she went on to establish Funding U, a company designed to provide education loans to students who might struggle to qualify for conventional private lending because they do not have a cosigner.The connection between the two women is striking largely because the original loan was so ordinary. Tarkenton had helped someone she knew personally. Later, she applied a similar principle on a much larger scale to students facing financial barriers.Funding U has since provided about $80 million in low-interest loans to roughly 8,000 students, according to Princeton.Tarkenton has been reluctant to portray herself as the person responsible for Scott’s later success. In an interview with the Princeton Alumni Weekly, she suggested that Scott would probably have found a way to finish university anyway.Her point was less about claiming credit than about recognising how small acts of assistance can accumulate. For Scott, the $1,000 mattered because it arrived at a moment when she needed it.The $1,000 loan became part of Scott’s larger giving philosophyScott’s philanthropic approach has grown into something far removed from that college loan. Through Yield Giving, the platform she established in 2022, she has directed billions of dollars to thousands of organisations.Her method has also attracted attention because many of the recipients are relatively small or community-based groups rather than only the largest charitable institutions. The money is often intended to give organisations room to decide how best to use it.By early 2026, Scott had given roughly $26 billion through her philanthropy, according to Fortune, while continuing to hold a large personal fortune.Yet when Scott reflected on what had shaped her attitude towards giving, she did not point only to the enormous sums involved. She remembered individual people.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jason Arday Death: Nathan Cofnas, who exposed Cambridge scholar's plagiarism, under-fire at his university
articles.summary: UK News: Nathan Cofnas, who exposed Jason Arday’s plagiarism, faces ‘appropriate action’ from Ghent University after Arday’s deathGhent University has announce.
articles.body: Nathan Cofnas, who exposed Jason Arday’s plagiarism, faces ‘appropriate action’ from Ghent University after Arday’s deathGhent University has announced it will take “appropriate action” against one of its postdoctoral researchers, Nathan Cofnas, following the death of Cambridge professor Jason Arday. Cofnas, a philosopher of biology employed at the Belgian university, publicly detailed extensive evidence of plagiarism in Arday’s academic work in a Substack post published in late July 2026. Arday, who had been celebrated as Cambridge’s youngest Black professor, resigned from his position in early August amid growing scrutiny. He was later found dead. In a statement issued on 19 August 2026, Ghent University said it was “shocked” by Arday’s death and that it was taking Cofnas’s recent public statements on the matter “very seriously.”Nathan Cofnas’s plagiarism allegations against Jason ArdayIn July 2026, Nathan Cofnas published a detailed analysis on his Substack newsletter claiming that large portions of Jason Arday’s 2015 PhD thesis contained material closely matching or identical to earlier work by other scholars, including a 2009 dissertation by Paula Zwozdiak-Myers. Cofnas also raised questions about other aspects of Arday’s published research and biographical claims. The post attracted significant attention and was followed by further reporting in British media outlets examining Arday’s academic record.Arday acknowledged certain citation errors but denied intentional misconduct, attributing some issues to inadequate supervision during his doctoral studies and his autism. Cambridge University initially defended him against what it described as a campaign to undermine his credibility. On 5–6 August 2026, however, the university announced it was opening an investigation into his academic qualifications and honorary appointments. Arday resigned shortly afterwards.Arday’s death and public reactionJason Arday was found dead in mid-August 2026. His death prompted widespread discussion and tributes, as well as criticism directed at those who had publicised the plagiarism allegations. Some activists and online campaigns specifically targeted Cofnas, urging people to contact Ghent University and hold him responsible for the outcome. Reports indicated organised efforts to send mass complaints to the university.Ghent University’s statementOn 19 August 2026, Ghent University issued an official statement signed by Rector Petra De Sutter and Vice-Rector Herwig Reynaert. The university expressed shock at Arday’s death and offered condolences. It reaffirmed its commitment to respect for human dignity and opposition to discrimination, hatred, and racism, while stating that academic freedom “is not unlimited” and “goes hand in hand with responsibility.”The statement confirmed that the university was taking the recent public statements made by a postdoctoral researcher (Cofnas) “very seriously” and had “decided to take appropriate action within its powers and the applicable framework.” Officials emphasised that they did not wish to prejudge any decisions in order to maintain objectivity and respect the confidentiality of a personnel matter.The full statement is available on the university’s website.Context surrounding CofnasNathan Cofnas joined Ghent University as a postdoctoral researcher in 2026. He has previously attracted controversy for his writings on hereditarianism and group differences in intelligence, positions he describes as “race realist.” His appointment at Ghent had already drawn petitions and criticism from some staff and students earlier in the year. The current university response focuses specifically on his public comments regarding the Arday case. As of 20 August 2026, Ghent University has not provided further details on the nature or timeline of the “appropriate action” it intends to take.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Chandigarh was built as a planned city. So why does it keep sinking in the rain?
articles.summary: CHANDIGARH: Chandigarh was designed to be different — a city of sectors, wide roads, planned green spaces and carefully engineered infrastructure.Yet,.
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: Chandigarh was designed to be different — a city of sectors, wide roads, planned green spaces and carefully engineered infrastructure.Yet, every monsoon, the same question returns: how can a city built around such meticulous planning repeatedly turn into a maze of flooded roads, stranded vehicles and submerged markets? Tuesday’s deluge offered another uncomfortable answer.A mere two hours of intense rain was enough to expose how vulnerable parts of the city have become.72.4mm and the city starts to sinkThe city got 72.4mm of rain in just two hours, the heaviest two-hour downpour of the current monsoon season.What followed was something familiar but harder to ignore as an occasional monsoon quirk: roads turned into rivers, cars were stranded in waist-high water, houses and shops were flooded and thousands of commuters were stuck in traffic jams.The worst affected stretches were not in one corner of Chandigarh. Rapid water accumulation was reported in Sectors 17, 22, 24, 36, 37, 42 and 43, as well as along Jan Marg, Madhya Marg, Industrial Area Phases I and II, Hallomajra and areas around the Old Secretariat.Water seeped into corridors and basements of Sector 22, one of the busiest commercial centers of the city, flooded parking areas and shopkeepers had to resort to flex boards, mops and rags to keep water out.When roads in Chandigarh are no longer roadsMore troubling was the state of the city’s traffic network. Vehicles crawled through submerged stretches, bumper-to-bumper, two-wheelers struggled to negotiate potholes and hidden manholes and many cars broke down while trying to cross flooded junctions.Ambulances heading to PGIMER were reportedly stranded on Madhya Marg, showing how quickly a waterlogging problem can turn into an emergency-services crisis.Residents also complained about the poor management of traffic when it was most needed. Police personnel were said to be scarce on parts of Madhya Marg, including the stretch between Transport Light Point and the IAF Museum light point.Some places saw barricades coming up but commuters said there was little on-ground help to divert traffic or guide motorists through alternate routes. In a city where traffic was normally orderly, the lack of visible intervention became a problem in itself.A road literally washed awayThe rain didn’t just flood roads, it wrecked one. A portion of the carriageway on Madhya Marg between Transport Light Point and Grain Market Chowk reportedly caved in or washed away, forcing the traffic police to divert traffic coming from Panchkula through the road behind Police Lines toward ITI Light Point.The incident pointed to another vulnerability, that of road infrastructure itself becoming the next victim if drainage systems fail.Downed trees and limbs also added to the disruption. Trees or branches had fallen on the roads in several places, including Sector 22, making the already congested carriageways narrower and posing additional hazards.It was not just that motorists would be late getting home. Residents said a badly clogged or blocked road can delay ambulances, fire trucks and other emergency vehicles when every second counts.City’s drainage problem predates Tuesday rainThus, the problem of Chandigarh is not that it rained. The problem is that known amounts of rain still result in predictable failures in known places.The Municipal Corporation undertakes cleaning and desilting of road gullies and storm water drains before the monsoon every year. But several waterlogging hotspots keep flooding.This means that cleaning alone cannot compensate for an aging or inadequate drainage network.The figures offer us a useful context. According to Central Ground Water Board data, Chandigarh receives an annual average rainfall of about 1,009.8mm, of which about 844.9mm falls during the monsoon.So, the city’s drainage infrastructure has to cope with serious seasonal rainfall, not freak events, as a basic design parameter.It is not just a case of ‘too much rain’Another irony. In fact, Chandigarh had a rainfall deficit earlier in the monsoon. The city received 240.2mm till July 25, against the normal of 359.6mm for June-July, a deficit of around 33%.July itself had 200.9mm against a normal of 204mm. The lesson is a good one: a city doesn’t need a season’s worth of excess rain to flood. And a short furious spell can swamp the system if rain falls faster than the water can drain away.But the problem is no longer confined to Chandigarh. Residents across Mohali, Zirakpur, Kharar and Nayagaon were in the same familiar cycle on Tuesday.In Mohali’s Sector 70 and Phase 11, school buses, cars, two-wheelers and pedestrians were seen passing through stagnant water on waterlogged streets.Not only were flooded roads an inconvenience for children and elderly residents, they also increased the risk of slips and falls and exposure to unhygienic stagnant water.Planned city, unplanned outcome?This is where the larger conversation on Chandigarh’s monsoon problem is needed. The city was planned, zoned and built with infrastructure in mind.But a city planned with infrastructure for an earlier era may become vulnerable when asked to cope with today’s rainfall intensity, traffic volumes, construction patterns and expanding urbanization. The thing is not that the drains were cleaned before the monsoon.The question that has become is whether the entire storm-water system still holds up for the city of Chandigarh.So the flooding on Tuesday should not end with water being pumped out, fallen trees cleared and the damaged carriageway repaired.These are essential emergency responses, but they are not a flood management strategy. The real test is whether the administration can identify all recurring hotspots, map drainage capacity against rainfall intensity, clear bottlenecks and redesign vulnerable stretches before the next cloudburst does the audit for it.Because the problem with Chandigarh is not that it has never been planned. It’s that the city has changed faster than some of the infrastructure under it.If 72.4mm of rain in two hours can bring Sector 17, Sector 22, Madhya Marg and several peripheral areas to a halt, the question for policymakers is not when will it rain again.How many more monsoons will it take for Chandigarh’s drainage system to catch up to the city it was meant to serve?You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: In 1990, Utah used the world’s largest rotenone treatment on Strawberry Reservoir; over 99% of fish biomass vanished and the rebuilt fishery later produced 715,000 catches a year
articles.summary: US News: In August 1990, Utah wildlife officials carried out one of the largest chemical fish-removal projects in fisheries history, wiping out almost every fi.
articles.body: In August 1990, Utah wildlife officials carried out one of the largest chemical fish-removal projects in fisheries history, wiping out almost every fish in Utah’s Strawberry Reservoir to save its collapsing ecosystem. The operation, led by the Utah Division of Wildlife Resources (UDWR) and described in publications from the American Fisheries Society and UDWR research reports, removed more than 99 per cent of the lake’s total fish biomass. By clearing out the non-native fish, biologists were able to rebuild the food web and create a healthier sport fishery that later produced more than 715,000 angler catches a year. Located 23 miles east of Heber City, the high-elevation reservoir had long been one of the Intermountain West’s best cold-water fishing destinations. But by the late 1980s, large numbers of introduced Utah chub (Gila atraria) and redside shiners had overwhelmed native game fish. They consumed much of the available plankton and contributed to a major decline in trout numbers.Overwhelmed reservoir needed a drastic resetWildlife managers had already tried a smaller rotenone treatment at the original Strawberry Reservoir in 1961. But when Soldier Creek Dam expanded the reservoir in 1973, increasing its surface area to more than 17,000 acres, illegally introduced Utah chub quickly spread through the newly flooded areas. By 1989, UDWR gill-net surveys showed how serious the problem had become. Non-native forage fish made up more than 90 per cent of the total fish weight in the reservoir. Attempts to stock trout were failing. Millions of hatchery-raised trout fry were either eaten by adult chubs or struggled to find enough food because of competition for tiny aquatic organisms. With the reservoir becoming less productive and fewer people visiting to fish, state biologists concluded that partial netting, commercial fishing and biological controls would not solve the problem. A complete chemical treatment was considered the only practical way to clear the lake.Military-scale operation across huge watershedThe project required a major logistical effort involving hundreds of people from state and federal agencies. The treatment covered the 17,000-acre reservoir, its many bays and more than 170 miles of streams flowing into the Strawberry River drainage. To reduce the amount of chemical needed and lower costs, water managers first lowered the reservoir to its lowest operating level. Crews then applied rotenone, a plant-based chemical that stops cellular respiration in fish and other gill-breathing organisms and breaks down quickly in sunlight. According to historical American Fisheries Society records, teams used heavy machinery, specialised barges, deep-water pumps, all-terrain vehicles and aircraft to spread thousands of gallons of liquid rotenone and dry powder. Dripper stations were placed along mountain streams to make sure the chemical reached side channels, marshes, springs and beaver ponds connected to the main reservoir. Within days, the treatment moved through the entire system. Millions of Utah chub, redside shiners and other non-native fish died and either washed onto the shore or sank to the lake bottom. Follow-up biological surveys showed that more than 99 per cent of the reservoir’s fish biomass had been removed, leaving the lake with a largely empty food web that could be rebuilt.Predatory trout restore the balanceAfter the chemical naturally broke down in late autumn 1990, UDWR began a large restocking programme aimed at preventing non-native fish from taking over again. Biologists introduced millions of native Bear Lake cutthroat trout (Oncorhynchus clarki utah) along with sterile rainbow trout. Bear Lake cutthroat were chosen because they become strong fish-eaters as adults. Unlike earlier trout strains used in the reservoir, the cutthroat naturally prey on smaller fish in open water. This gave the lake a permanent predator that could help control any Utah chub that survived the treatment. The plan worked. With less competition for food, the stocked cutthroat grew quickly. By the mid-1990s, fishing records and UDWR surveys showed a major recovery. State fishery data recorded annual catches of up to 715,000 trout during peak years. Strawberry Reservoir regained its reputation as one of Utah’s top trout fisheries, drawing more than one million angler hours each year and generating tens of millions of dollars for the local economy.Barriers protect the recoveryTo protect the recovery, UDWR built permanent fish traps and barriers along important spawning streams, including the Strawberry River and Indian Creek. The structures allow biologists to catch, count and sort spawning fish while preventing non-native species from moving upstream to reproduce. Today, strict fishing rules and slot limits help protect large predatory cutthroat trout, ensuring enough mature fish remain to keep chub numbers under control. The 1990 Strawberry Reservoir treatment remains an important example of modern freshwater management. It showed that large-scale chemical fish removal, combined with carefully planned predator stocking, can restore a heavily damaged aquatic ecosystem.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: US Streamers News: Sonia Bellina’s sudden death has left her family and more than 260,000 TikTok followers searching for answers after her body was discovered burned in .
articles.body: Sonia Bellina’s sudden death has left her family and more than 260,000 TikTok followers searching for answers after her body was discovered burned in a French vineyard. The 29-year-old creator had built a following through lip-sync videos and personal content, but her final days have now become the focus of a murder investigation. Two men were detained in connection with the case, although one has since been released.Who was Sonia Bellina and what is her cause of death?Bellina was a French social media creator known for her TikTok presence, where she had attracted a sizable audience with lip-sync clips and other videos. Her online following made news of her disappearance particularly distressing for fans who had watched her content.According to French prosecutors, Bellina was reported missing on Aug. 10. Two days later, a farm worker discovered a burned body lying between rows of vines in Saint-Gilles, near Nîmes. Investigators later identified the remains as Bellina through DNA testing.Her family had already feared the body belonged to her. Bellina’s relatives told French outlet Midi Libre that personal details, including her breast implants and a ring, appeared to match those of the woman found in the vineyard.The discovery prompted a murder investigation. Authorities scheduled an autopsy, although prosecutors have not publicly released detailed findings about Bellina’s cause or manner of death.The circumstances surrounding her final hours remain unclear, leaving investigators to piece together what happened after she left home.Sonia Bellina death investigation leads to two arrestsThe Nîmes Prosecutor’s Office said two men were arrested because investigators had evidence suggesting their direct or indirect involvement in the incident. However, authorities later confirmed that one of the men had been released from custody.The remaining suspect was kept in detention after prosecutors received an extension through Aug. 21. Authorities said further information would be released after that point.The arrests do not establish guilt. The investigation remains active, and the circumstances surrounding Bellina’s death have yet to be fully established by prosecutors.Bellina’s family has also spoken publicly about the loss. Her sister said during a TikTok live that Bellina had told relatives she was going out one evening but never returned. The family had reportedly been preparing to celebrate her 30th birthday on Sept. 30.Instead, they are now mourning her death while waiting for investigators to determine what happened.Her sister also pushed back against cruel comments appearing online after Bellina’s death. She said some people had posted hurtful claims about the influencer and urged users to stop speculating while the family grieves.The case has drawn attention not only because of Bellina’s online following but also because of the disturbing circumstances in which her body was discovered. For now, investigators are working to establish a clear timeline, determine how Bellina died and understand what led to her remains being left in the vineyard.As the investigation continues, the family’s search for answers remains at the heart of the case. Further updates from French authorities could provide crucial details about the final hours of the TikTok creator’s life and the circumstances behind her death.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Mark Zuckerberg buys Gothic castle in Ireland, Meta's international headquarters, for $35 million
articles.summary: Tech News News: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and wife Priscilla Chan have bought Strancally Castle, a Gothic-style mansion in Ireland, for an estimated $35 million, accor.
articles.body: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and wife Priscilla Chan have bought Strancally Castle, a Gothic-style mansion in Ireland, for an estimated $35 million, according to reports. The historic property sits on a 178-hectare (440-acre) estate in County Waterford and will serve as a base for the couple when they visit Ireland. The purchase also has a connection to Meta, which maintains its international headquarters in Ireland. A Meta spokesperson said Mark Zuckerberg and his family are looking forward to caring for the historic property and spending time in the country.The exact amount paid for the castle has not been made public. The Irish Times estimated its value at between €20 million and €30 million.Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg's Ireland homeStrancally Castle was built in 1830 for John Keily, a former Conservative MP. Architects James and George Richard Pain designed the property on a large scale. The castle is part of a 440-acre estate in County Waterford. According to the book The Houses of Ireland, the size of the property was such that it once took a few minutes to walk from the dining room to the kitchen.The property was bought and renovated in the early 2000s by Michael Alen-Buckley, co-founder of investment firm RAB Capital, and his wife, Giancarla. The couple said they were pleased that Zuckerberg and his family planned to continue maintaining the property.Why Mark Zuckerberg bought the castleMark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan are expected to use Strancally Castle as their base when visiting Ireland. The purchase also comes as Meta maintains its international headquarters in Ireland, making the country an important location for the company.“Mark and his family are excited to continue caring for this historic home and look forward to spending time in Ireland, where Meta maintains its international headquarters,” a Meta spokesperson was quoted as saying.Strancally Castle is located in the Blackwater Valley, an area known for historic estates. The National Built Heritage Service, an Irish state agency, describes the castle as having sandstone and limestone construction and highlights its stonework and craftsmanship.“The construction in sandstone and limestone ashlar augments the dour tone of the composition while providing evidence of high quality stone masonry and craftsmanship,” it says.The area is also home to other properties owned by wealthy business figures. Entrepreneur James Dyson bought Ballynatray House in 2024, while Stripe co-founder John Collison bought Abbey Leix in County Laois in 2021.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: In 2016, the Burt's Bees co-founder gave the US 87,500 acres and backed it with $40 million; 10 years later the Maine wilderness is a national monument
articles.summary: US News: Roxanne Quimby has had a life for the books. The woman who has held multiple roles including that of an artist, homesteader, mother, storyteller, phil.
articles.body: Roxanne Quimby has had a life for the books. The woman who has held multiple roles including that of an artist, homesteader, mother, storyteller, philanthropist and entrepreneur is the face behind what is possibly the world's best-known lip balm brand. One that floods every woman's Pinterest board and definitely her cart. While Quimby may be known for her business, what she is also known for is donations of Maine woodlands to the US government in order to protect the land, which later became a national monument, as per the Burt's Bees website.The finding of a businesswomanWhile her sisters followed in their father's footsteps and went to business school, Roxanne drove cross-country from New England to go to art school to fulfil a dream she had since the age of five. After completing art school, she and her boyfriend George bought and fixed up a van and headed back to Vermont in search of land and to try their hand at self-sufficient living. They found thirty acres for the right price in Guilford, Maine and with no running water or electricity, they set out building a cabin, growing their own food, chopping their own wood and eventually raising twins. “It was an idyllic time—we never fought about what to watch on TV,” remembered Roxanne. Roxanne waitressed a couple shifts a week and George worked a couple days at the local radio station to cover minimal expenses, but they were deep in the DIY existence for seven years.Soon, the lifestyle began to wear on Roxanne and her marriage. “It didn’t provide enough stimulation for my personality,” shared Roxanne, “I’m kind of restless and a pretty curious person and interested in the way the world works.” It was the early ‘80s and the twins were six when she moved out of the cabin, determined to find a way to provide a good education for them, as her parents had for her.It was in the summer of '83 that Roxanne was hitchhiking when she met Burt Shavitz, known around town as the local 'bee man' who sold honey roadside from his yellow pickup truck. She was intrigued by Burt, and they struck up a friendship where she would learn about beekeeping and, in exchange, help Burt with his hives. “He was an inspiration for how one could live—very independently and with their own unique set of rules,” recalls Roxanne.When she met Burt, his honey was packaged in reused gallon pickle jars from the local diner. After a summer of apprenticeship, Roxanne, ever the artist, suggested they package the honey in smaller containers with bespoke labels to sell at craft fairs, which were a big hit.When she discovered his 200-pound stash of leftover beeswax, she got busy learning to make beeswax candles in cute shapes like teddy bears and fruit. They decided on the name ‘Burt’s Bees’, mimicking a stamp Burt put on his hives to prevent theft. After a boutique in NYC started selling their candles in the late eighties, business really picked up. They introduced a Beeswax skincare line, including the famous Beeswax Lip Balm in a refillable terra-cotta pot, to their product lineup.The brand's operations grew from Roxanne's kitchen, old school house, and old bowling alley, until they had to move out of Maine altogether. She moved Burt’s Bees to North Carolina for a more business-friendly atmosphere.For the love of the landEven when the brand moved to North Carolina, Roxanne kept the ties to Maine, commuting back and forth. Inspired by the essays of naturalist Henry David Thoreau, who spent time in the North Maine Woods, she became interested in preserving the woodlands just north of where the brand got its start. She even used the Burt’s Bees catalogue to promote the idea of a Maine Woods National Park, encouraging customers to get involved.In 1998, Roxanne purchased her first land in Maine with the aim of one day being able to create a national park in the same region that inspired Thoreau more than 150 years earlier. Since the end of the last Ice Age 12,000 years ago, the waterways, wildlife, flora and fauna, night skies, and other resources have attracted people to the area. Artists, authors, scientists, conservationists and others, including Teddy Roosevelt, Henry David Thoreau and John James Audubon –have also drawn knowledge and inspiration from the area's resources.She continued to purchase land over time, with the goal of having it designated and protected. As the company grew more profitable, Roxanne sold 80% of her stake and continued to invest in land for conservation. From 2001 – 2003, she spent $8 million to buy huge parcels of undeveloped land in northern Maine, nearly 16,000 acres in total. She continued acquiring land, against quite strong opposition from logging communities who were using the forests and rivers to feed paper mills.In 2016, on the eve of the 100th anniversary of the National Park Service, Roxanne donated 87,500 acres of “awe-inspiring mountains, forests and waters” in Maine’s North Woods to be designated and federally protected as Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument. The land gift was valued at $60 million and came with a $20 million endowment from Roxanne to support infrastructure development and operations. "In Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument, you feel connected to something bigger than yourself. I can think of no better thing to do with Burt's Bees profits than to return them to the earth," she said.Back then, U.S. Secretary of the Interior Sally Jewell and National Park Service Director Jonathan B. Jarvis applauded President Obama's designation of the Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument, the first national monument to preserve the landscape and honour the history and culture of Maine's North Woods. "As the National Park Service begins a second century of conservation this week, the President's designation of Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument serves as an inspiration to reflect on America's iconic landscapes and historical and cultural treasures," said Secretary Jewell. "Through this incredibly generous private gift for conservation, these lands will remain accessible to current and future generations of Americans, ensuring the rich history of Mainers' hunting, fishing and recreation heritage will forever be preserved."Friends of Katahdin Woods and Waters, the National Park Service and the Elliotsville Foundation have worked closely with members of the Penobscot, Maliseet, Passamaquoddy and Mi’kmaq Nations to include Indigenous knowledge and perspectives in the development and stewardship of the Monument.In 2020, the International Dark-Sky Association recognised Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument as the first International Dark Sky Sanctuary on the US eastern seaboard and only the 12th such site in the world. The designation reflects how the value of a place can change over time.What are your views on this? Tell us in the comments section below.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: Park Geonroung, the child star of Pinkfong's "Baby Shark Dance", has made his K-pop debut a decade after appearing in the viral video.The 2016 video, in which Park appeared at the age of 7, has more than 17.2 billion views and remains the most-watched video in YouTube history.Now 17, Park released his first digital single, "WAVE", on Thursday under the stage name Baby Shark Boy, with backing from The Pinkfong Company, which turned Baby Shark into a global entertainment franchise.The Guardian reported that "Baby Shark Dance" has held YouTube's No. 1 position for 69 consecutive months."Baby Shark Dance brought joy to people around the world, and I'm very grateful that so many people still remember me from 10 years ago. That made me want to come back and connect with people through music again," Park told Reuters.Baby Shark melody returns in 'WAVE'The Baby Shark tune features at the beginning of "WAVE" before the song moves into electropop with trap elements. Park also contributed to the lyrics, which Pinkfong said draw on his return after 10 years and his decision to take on a new challenge.The track features Joohoney of K-pop group Monsta X. Young-jun Choi led TEAM SAME on the choreography. Choi has previously worked with acts including BTS, Seventeen and Twice. Pinkfong said some movements associated with the original Baby Shark dance have been adapted for the K-pop performance.Despite growing up as the face of a video watched billions of times, Park told The Guardian that his childhood remained largely normal. However, the song itself was difficult to escape. Park recalled that Baby Shark became so familiar that he would sometimes find himself humming it without realising.Pinkfong's 2016 video spawned parodies and a dance craze. The song was later played at the White House, while US President Donald Trump and Tesla CEO Elon Musk were among those who praised it. Park remained associated with Pinkfong after the original video and appeared in other programmes produced by the company. "WAVE", however, marks his first solo K-pop digital single.Park said he sees "WAVE" as the start of a longer musical journey and hopes to show different sides of himself through music and other content.Pinkfong is also making "WAVE: Becoming Baby Shark Boy", a documentary about Park's journey from child performer to his new musical identity and the making of his debut single. articles.title: Rompimento de contrato fecha creches em São Miguel Arcanjo | G1
articles.standfirst: Merendeiras protestaram diante da Secretaria de Educação, cobrando salários e benefícios atrasados pela antiga empresa contratada. Prefeitura informou que pretende solucionar a situação até quinta-feira (19).
articles.summary: Creches de São Miguel Arcanjo (SP) fecharam temporariamente nesta segunda-feira (16). A prefeitura rescindiu o contrato com a empresa fornecedora de merenda escolar.
articles.body:
As creches municipais de São Miguel Arcanjo (SP) foram fechadas temporariamente após a prefeitura rescindir o contrato com a empresa fornecedora de merenda na cidade, nesta segunda-feira (16).

Um grupo com cerca de 50 merendeiras se reuniu com representantes do sindicato da área nesta segunda-feira, em frente à Secretaria de Educação, e cobrou providências da prefeitura, já que a empresa atual havia apresentado problemas.

Com o rompimento do contrato, as funcionárias estão com medo de não receberem os direitos trabalhistas. Para a merendeira Luana Silva, a situação tem sido motivo de preocupação e dúvidas.

"Eu levanto de casa 5h30 e tenho que estar na escola para trabalhar todos os dias, faça sol, chuva, doente ou não. Todas as meninas estão lá. Nós temos alunos que amamos e são como nossos filhos. Só que, para chegar nesse ponto, não podemos pensar somente neles. Também temos os nossos direitos", desabafa.

Rompimento de contrato leva ao fechamento de creches em São Miguel Arcanjo (SP) — Foto: Ricardo Kern/TV TEM

A representante do SindiRefeições, Alessandra Bércio, afirma que houve atrasos de salários e benefícios, mesmo com o contrato estando ativo há poucos meses.

"Em poucos meses de vigência, houve atraso de salário e de benefício. O sindicato notificou, cobrou, sem saber se vão receber ou qual empresa vai assumir", detalha.

Márcia Aparecida Nunes também é uma das merendeiras afetadas pela falta de pagamentos. Ela afirma que, até o momento, não recebeu uma série de direitos trabalhistas, como o 13º salário.

"Não estavam pagando certo e assim foi ficando cada dia pior. Eu ainda não recebi o pagamento de outubro. Agora, recebemos a notícia da prefeitura de que não receberíamos vale, 13º, pagamento, nada. Nem férias", lamenta.

Márcia Aparecida Nunes também é uma das merendeiras afetadas pela falta de pagamentos — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

Enquanto uma nova empresa não é contratada, as escolas municipais receberão a chamada merenda seca, que é o alimento que não precisa de preparo na cozinha. Diante disso, algumas famílias estão adotando alternativas para as crinças que ficarão sem aulas.

Na casa de Roseli Almeida, que é cuidadora de idosos, apenas um dos cinco filhos foi à escola nesta segunda-feira. Os outros quatro não puderam ir à creche e, agora, a mãe precisa redobrar a atenção dentro da residência.

"Tem que ficar com 'um olho aqui e outro lá', pois cuido de uma senhora e tem que manter o almoço. Eu não posso simplesmente chegar e falar que não vou. Não é um problema dela. Os filhos são meus e eu tenho que dar meu jeito", afirma.

Roseli tem sofrido com a situação — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

À TV TEM , a Prefeitura de São Miguel Arcanjo informou que pretende fechar até quinta-feira (19) contrato com uma nova empresa para servir merenda emergencialmente. Entretanto, a gestão não deu detalhes sobre o rompimento do contrato e nem sobre como será feita a nova contratação.

A reportagem também procurou a Soluções Recursos Humanos, responsável pelo fornecimento da merenda, mas não obteve retorno até a publicação desta reportgem.

articles.title: Cobertura vacinal: Goianira está no top 3 do ranking nacional | G1
articles.standfirst: Sucesso da campanha é atribuído à capacitação das equipes e à busca ativa pela população. Com cobertura vacinal superior a 107%, município investe em horários estendidos e visitas escolares.
articles.summary: Com busca ativa e postos abertos até as 22h, Goianira alcança 107% de cobertura vacinal e ocupa a terceira posição no ranking nacional de imunização em 2025.
articles.body:
O Estado de Goiás está no pódio das cidades com maior cobertura vacinal do país. Goianira , na Região Metropolitana de Goiânia , é a primeira colocada no Centro-Oeste e ocupa a terceira posição no ranking nacional. Segundo a Secretaria de Saúde do município, atualmente Goianira tem seis postos de vacinação funcionando até o período noturno, além de equipes que vão até onde a população está.

Goianira tem cerca de 80 mil habitantes nos dados oficiais, mas a população total ultrapassa esse número; por isso, na contagem, a cobertura vacinal supera 107%. Entre os grupos mais vacinados estão as crianças e as gestantes. Vacinas contra hepatite B, BCG e meningite aparecem com mais de 100% de cobertura em cada uma.

A Secretaria de Saúde da cidade informou que conta com 22 unidades de saúde, sendo que seis funcionam das 16h às 22h, para atender as pessoas que não têm tempo de procurar os postos durante o dia.

Aldenia Sabino, secretária de Saúde de Goianira, conversou com a TV Anhanguera e disse que a cidade utiliza o Programa Saúde na Escola (PSE), do Governo Federal, para atuar dentro das instituições de ensino. " Temos a agenda e, todas as semanas, com as vacinas disponíveis, fazemos as visitas e o nosso trabalho de vacinação nas escolas", afirmou .

Para Aldenia, o índice que colocou a cidade em destaque começou com a capacitação dos profissionais que trabalham diretamente com a imunização. Segundo ela, outro trabalho fundamental feito no município é a conscientização da população.

"É necessário que nós estejamos prontos para ir a qualquer lugar, não só sermos procurados. Nós temos 22 equipes de saúde da família, todas com sala de vacinação. A gente não só espera receber, a gente vai atrás", disse.

Os números divulgados no ranking levam em consideração os dados colhidos em 2025, referentes a 11 vacinas, mas a secretária adiantou que, neste mês, mais novidades podem chegar.
